title: Billing explainability indexer for token-level provenance
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Motivation: Finance and customer success teams need a fast, queryable way to explain why a given invoice shows N tokens and how those tokens map to routes, model variants, batching decisions, and any late-arrival corrections. This ticket implements an indexer that consumes token-metering events and materializes explainability traces keyed by session-id / request-id.
acceptance_criteria: Indexer consumes production metering topic (proto v2) and persists explainability records to the billing_explainability store within 2x event arrival latency

Each explainability record contains: request_id, tenant_id, timestamp, token_count_by_bucket (model_variant, route, quantization_profile), routing_decisions, cache_hits, batch_id, and cost_estimate reference
Query API: Console trace endpoint can return explainability record for any invoice line within 30s of request and show breadcrumbs linking to underlying raw events
Backfill: we can backfill past 14 days of metering events without duplicating charges or changing billing outputs
Unit and integration tests exercise late-arrival replays and idempotency for at-least-once ingestion
Telemetry: SLI for indexer lag < 60s 99th percentile and error rate < 0.1% after warmup
tasks: Define stable explainability record schema and map to existing ledger fields
Implement consumer with windowed de-dup and deterministic merge logic
Add routing_decision enrichment using smart-routing snapshots service
Persist to new readonly billing_explainability store (partitioned by tenant_id/date)
Expose read API on console backend with tenant-scoped auth checks
Create backfill job and dry-run mode to validate against historical invoices
Write end-to-end tests and a small canary deployment to 3 low-volume tenants
